<p class="eyebrow">Research programme</p>

# Microbial ecology across scales.

My work connects descriptive metagenomics with mechanistic ecology and ecosystem engineering. The aim is not merely to identify microbial signatures, but to understand states, predict trajectories and design interventions.
:::

::: {.bento}
::: {.tile .wide}
<span class="num">01</span>

### Microbiome states and global branches

How can high-dimensional microbiome variation be represented as interpretable ecological states? Population metagenomics reveals recurrent configurations while longitudinal observations expose the transitions between them.
:::

::: {.tile .dark}
<span class="num">02</span>

### Stability and interaction mechanisms

Which resource constraints, interactions and historical contingencies determine whether a community resists, shifts or collapses?
:::

::: {.tile}
<span class="num">03</span>

### Food–gut ecosystem coalescence

Fermented foods are living microbial ecosystems. I investigate what happens when their communities and functions meet those of the human gut.
:::

::: {.tile .wide .acid}
<span class="num">04</span>

### Designed ecosystems

Ecological chassis, synthetic consortia and digital twins provide complementary ways to test causal hypotheses and steer microbial fluxes.
:::
:::

::: {.section}
## Scientific trajectory

Pasteur Institute and nutritional gut ecology shaped my experimental foundations; EMBL and MetaGenoPolis expanded them to population metagenomics; Danone added translational research; INRAE Micalis now provides the setting to connect food microbial ecology with ecosystem engineering.
:::
